threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still flinch every time the bus driver shouts ‘get on!’ instead of waiting for you to sit down. You’ll learn soon enough.
Caught a night bus to Brixton, and a guy in a parka serenaded the whole route with off-key Bohemian Rhapsody. The drivers just sighed, but we loved it.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I saw a guy jogging with a beer in hand, weaving through families and street art. That’s the spirit of Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Kreuzberg's hidden U-Bahn stations have graffiti art that turns commuting into a mini gallery tour. It's like traveling through an urban museum daily.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only a true local knows to carry dog biscuits after 5 pm to appease the pack of strays around Dolores Park. They’ll block your path otherwise.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a full tuxedo hopping on the 21 tonight, carrying a bouquet of flowers. Street style is peak San Francisco.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all locals love 'festa major' noise, but many of us dread the late-night fireworks keeping our kids up.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by the way they ask for 'tapas' instead of 'platos pequeños'—typically a dead giveaway in Gràcia.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think a tube strike is just a minor inconvenience instead of the apocalypse it actually is.
Saw a guy trying to impress a girl by rapping about the bus route. She was laughing, but the bus driver wasn’t having it. Classic Brixton vibes.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I stumbled upon an underground pétanque court in a hidden park, I knew Neukölln had more surprises up its sleeve than I ever expected.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a hidden kebab stand with a line that wraps around the block, open till sunrise, serving the best post-party döner.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they nod at the taco truck guy like he’s family, even if they just ordered a burrito.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a tuxedo juggling outside the Civic Center station while Muni was delayed. Just another day in the city where anything can happen.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Most tourists think Gràcia is all about tourists. But the real charm? It's the hidden patios where locals sip vermut, not the busy squares.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by how they clutch a map in front of a bar, looking up and down the street as if waiting for a sign.
